items.followUp: Define stress and give its SI unit.

rubric.why: Shows that strain is a ratio of a change in dimension to the original dimension.
rubric.description: Strain is the ratio of the change in a dimension of a body to its original dimension.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving this ratio, such as extension divided by original length.

rubric.why: Explains why strain has no unit.
rubric.description: The numerator and denominator have the same units, so the units cancel and strain has no unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the units cancel or that strain is dimensionless.

modelAnswer: Strain = change in length / original length.
Both quantities have the same units, so the units cancel; therefore, strain is dimensionless and has no unit.

items.followUp: Define equilibrium and state the second condition of equilibrium.

rubric.why: Defines equilibrium as a state in which forces are balanced and the body's motion does not change.
rubric.description: A body is in equilibrium when the forces acting on it are balanced and its state of motion does not change.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a definition linking balanced forces or zero resultant force with no change in the body's state of motion.

rubric.why: States the first condition of equilibrium: the resultant force is zero.
rubric.description: The first condition of equilibrium is that the vector sum of all forces acting on a body is zero: ΣF = 0.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that the resultant or vector sum of the forces must be zero.

modelAnswer: A body is in equilibrium when the forces acting on it are balanced and its state of motion does not change.
The first condition of equilibrium is that the resultant force on the body is zero.
In symbols, the vector sum of all forces acting on the body is ΣF = 0.
